title: "Packaging Formats Compared: .deb, .rpm, .pkg.tar.zst, .apk"

# Packaging Formats Compared: .deb, .rpm, .pkg.tar.zst, .apk

The package format is the fundamental currency of a distribution. Stripped of branding, a package is simply an archive containing:
1. The compiled files to be installed into the filesystem (`/usr/bin`, `/usr/lib`, `/etc`).
2. Declarative metadata (package name, version, architecture, license, dependencies).
3. Optional maintainer hook scripts (pre-install, post-install, pre-removal, post-removal).

```
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
|                Package Anatomy Comparison                   |
|                                                             |
| Debian (.deb):       Standard Unix `ar` archive             |
|                      ├── debian-binary (format version 2.0) |
|                      ├── control.tar.xz (metadata + hooks)  |
|                      └── data.tar.xz (payload filesystem)   |
|                                                             |
| Red Hat (.rpm):      Custom binary lead + header + cpio payload
|                      ├── Lead & Signature block (GPG)       |
|                      ├── RPM Header (metadata tags)         |
|                      └── CPIO archive (payload compressed)  |
|                                                             |
| Arch (.pkg.tar.zst): Standard tarball compressed with Zstandard
|                      ├── .PKGINFO (plaintext metadata)      |
|                      ├── .INSTALL (optional shell hooks)    |
|                      ├── .MTREE (file checksums & perms)    |
|                      └── usr/... (payload directly at root) |
|                                                             |
| Alpine (.apk):       Gzip/Zstd tarball with custom tar headers
|                      ├── .PKGINFO                           |
|                      ├── .INSTALL                           |
|                      └── data files with SHA1 checksums     |
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
```

## Deconstructing Debian's `.deb` Format

Debian `.deb` packages use the standard UNIX `ar` archive utility, ensuring they can be inspected on any UNIX system without special tools:

```bash
# Extracting a .deb package manually using standard binutils:
$ ar -x curl_7.88.1-10_amd64.deb
$ ls -l
-rw-r--r-- 1 user user      4 debian-binary
-rw-r--r-- 1 user user   2144 control.tar.xz
-rw-r--r-- 1 user user 289412 data.tar.xz

# Inspecting the control metadata:
$ tar -xf control.tar.xz
$ cat control
Package: curl
Version: 7.88.1-10
Architecture: amd64
Maintainer: Debian curl team
Depends: libc6 (>= 2.34), libcurl4 (= 7.88.1-10), zlib1g (>= 1:1.1.4)
Description: command line tool for transferring data with URL syntax
```

## Deconstructing Arch Linux's `.pkg.tar.zst`

Arch Linux packages prioritize raw speed and simplicity. Instead of nesting archives, an Arch package is a single `tar` archive compressed using Facebook's high-speed **Zstandard (`zstd`)** algorithm:

```bash
# Decompressing and inspecting an Arch package:
$ tar --zstd -tf ripgrep-14.1.0-1-x86_64.pkg.tar.zst
.PKGINFO
.BUILDINFO
.MTREE
usr/
usr/bin/
usr/bin/rg
usr/share/man/man1/rg.1.gz
```

Because `.pkg.tar.zst` contains the actual filesystem tree directly at the root of the archive, package installation is as fast as unpacking a tarball directly into `/`!

## Deconstructing Alpine's `.apk` Format

Alpine's `apk` packages are designed for high-density, low-latency container environments:
- Compact headers and SHA1/SHA256 control hashes embedded directly in extended tar header fields.
- Extremely rapid decompression with minimal CPU overhead.
- No heavy Python or Perl runtime dependencies for package management: `apk-tools` is written in pure, static C.
